tasks.short: Explain to sites and HR how to code costs and stay inside the budget.

today.trigger: A site lead, an HR business partner or a bookkeeper asks how to code a cost, accrue agency hours or stay inside a site budget, usually by mail or in Teams.
steps: Read the question and find the current procedure on SharePoint.
Pull the site's actuals against budget from Power BI or an Excel export of AFAS.
Apply the rule on cost centres, accruals and CAO allowances, and note where the three sites differ.
Reply with the treatment and the budget that remains, then correct the posting if they already booked it.
Save the answer in the mail thread, where the next person cannot find it.
drudgery: Answering the same cost-centre question for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
Searching SharePoint for the latest version of a procedure.
Rebuilding a small actuals table that the nightly extract already holds.
today.time_sinks: Most of the time goes to finding the current rule and the current numbers, and to picking the thread up again after a close interruption.

lenses.faster: A draft answer comes back with the SharePoint procedure and last night's budget versus actuals already attached. Searching for the document and rebuilding the Excel snippet disappear.
lenses.autonomous: When a site crosses a budget threshold on the nightly refresh, or when a question matches a published coding line exactly, the draft opens on its own. New or conflicting questions wait for the controller.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, every site lead and HR business partner would get the same treatment the same day, and Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo would stop keeping three local habits.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses hunting for the latest coding note. The conversation worth keeping is the one with a site lead who is about to miss the labour budget.
lenses.options: The reply can show two or three treatments the procedure allows, with the effect of each on the site result, cash and the flex-versus-own-staff line.
lenses.altitude: The controller maintains the coding table, the examples and the exception list, and reviews the answers that the table cannot settle.
reach: First answers to cost-centre questions that budget holders now send to the FP&A analysts.
Coding questions on supplier and agency invoices that the bookkeepers now escalate one by one.
A costed view of a CAO allowance or an agency margin for an HR business partner writing a staffing case.

tasks.human_edge: The call when a real operation does not fit the written rule, and the conversation that gets a budget holder to act on it.
tasks.pattern_why: The result is direction that other units will follow. The procedure and the numbers can be assembled for the controller, and the controller still chooses the treatment and sends the answer.

in_practice.trigger: A budget holder or HR asks a coding or budget question in Teams, or a site's actuals cross a threshold on the nightly Power BI refresh.
steps: Retrieve the current procedure from SharePoint and the site's actuals versus budget from Power BI.
Draft the answer with the cost centre, the accrual and the budget that remains.
Attach the treatments the procedure allows, with the effect on the site result.
The controller edits the draft and sends it, or marks the case as a new exception.
Add the accepted repeat answer to the published coding table.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller sends every answer that chooses a treatment or tells a site it may spend. A published coding table can answer an exact lookup on its own.
data_needed: Current finance procedures and the cost-centre list
Budget and actuals by site and cost centre from the AFAS extract
CAO allowance codes and agency cost centres as they are booked in AFAS
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint library of finance answers, with the question, the documents used and the person who sent the reply.

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot can draft an answer from SharePoint files the user is allowed to open.
Power BI already holds finance dashboards on a nightly AFAS extract, so budget versus actual by site is a refresh, not a new system.
A large share of these questions repeat a written coding rule, and a smaller share needs a new judgment. The split at Noordhaven is not measured.

risks: A wrong treatment hits the month close and the forecast the business is asked to trust.
A stale SharePoint page can contradict the CAO or a local works-agreement on allowances.
If a Teams assistant answers staff directly, staff need to see that the draft was automatic and which procedure it used.
Budget and flex rates stay inside the Microsoft 365 tenant.
research_questions: What share of a quarter's questions is answered by a written rule, and what share needs a new judgment?
Are the procedures on SharePoint current for all three sites and for both CAOs?
How often does a coding answer later show up as a reclass or an audit adjustment?
Will site leads act on an answer that quotes the procedure and the numbers, without a meeting?

tasks.short: See where the result and the forecast moved, and what should improve.

today.trigger: The month's figures land, a site misses its labour or flex budget, or the finance director asks why the result moved against the forecast.
steps: Pull actuals from AFAS through the nightly Power BI extract and export the bridge to Excel.
Split movements by site, customer, own staff and flex, and compare them with the latest forecast.
Chase missing accruals for agency invoices, fuel, claims and dock overtime.
Write a short note on the causes and sit with FP&A and the site leads.
Correct the comment where the movement was a timing difference or a miscoding.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same variance bridge after every refresh.
Copying last month's commentary forward.
Tying agency-portal hours to the accrual in the ledger by hand.
today.time_sinks: The workbook breaks when a cost centre changes, and the note is written before the agency invoices and the accrual agree.

lenses.faster: When the nightly extract lands, the bridge by site and the flex-versus-own-staff split are already there, with a first comment on each line over the threshold. Building the workbook disappears.
lenses.autonomous: Each refresh files the movements over the threshold, including agency hours, claims, energy and overtime, on the close workspace. The controller opens a pack, not a blank file.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, every site and every large customer would have a weekly contribution view, and a flex, slotting or transport idea would be costed before the month is gone.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses pivoting the same cube. The work worth keeping is deciding which movement is a real operating issue and which is timing or coding.
lenses.options: The same result can be cut by site, by customer, by own staff versus flex, and by CAO allowance, each against a base, upside and downside forecast.
lenses.altitude: The controller owns the definitions of contribution, a fully loaded warehouse hour and the flex premium, and checks that the model still matches how AFAS is posted.
reach: The first variance pass the FP&A analysts now build for the forecast meeting.
A margin-versus-days-sales-outstanding flag for the credit and collections officer.
The flux lines the accountants now type into the close pack.

tasks.human_edge: Judgment on which movements are real, which are miscoding, and which operational change is worth asking a site to make.
tasks.pattern_why: The bridge and the first comments follow the ledger and a threshold. A conclusion that changes the forecast is sent only after the controller accepts each cause.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly AFAS extract refreshes in Power BI, and again when the monthly close starts.
steps: Refresh result, budget and forecast by site, customer, own staff and flex.
Flag lines over the controller's threshold, including agency cost, claims, energy and overtime.
Draft a cause from the account, the cost centre and the previous signed comment.
The controller accepts, corrects or drops each cause.
Send the signed note to FP&A and the site leads and store it with that forecast version.
in_practice.human_gate: No comment goes to the business until the controller has accepted each flagged cause.
data_needed: General-ledger actuals, budget and the current forecast version
Cost-centre and customer dimensions
Agency invoice accrual and hour totals
Prior signed commentary
in_practice.logs_to: The monthly close folder on SharePoint, stored next to the forecast version the note refers to.

evidence.claim: Power BI smart narrative writes a short summary of the numbers on a report page.
AFAS Profit reports actuals by cost centre, account and period, which is the population a variance bridge needs.
Agency hours sit in three separate portals and are not in the nightly AFAS extract, so the flex-premium cause still needs that tie-out.

risks: A pack that misses the agency accrual will describe a timing difference as an operational success and damage forecast trust.
A comment the controller has not signed will be read as finance's view.
Customer rates and agency margins stay inside the tenant.
Sickness cost can be discussed as a total. The Wet verbetering poortwachter file stays with HR and is not pulled into the finance note.
research_questions: What share of last quarter's material variances can be explained from AFAS dimensions alone?
How many days do agency invoices and Rabobank items lag the nightly extract, and did that lag change any story?
After three closes, did site leads use the signed notes, and did forecast accuracy move?
How many flagged lines were later reversed as miscoding?

tasks.short: Prepare the audit file and handle the auditor and the Belastingdienst.

today.trigger: The external accountant starts interim or year-end work, the Belastingdienst asks for support, or a finding from last year is still open.
steps: Agree the request list and the samples with the auditor.
Pull journals, revenue cutoff, agency accruals and bank lines from AFAS into Excel.
Chase Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo for proof of delivery, timesheets and agency hour backing.
Explain exceptions on cutoff, VAT on transport and the flex accrual.
Track findings and draft the management response for the finance director.
drudgery: Renaming exports to the request-list index.
Tying sample invoices back to the general ledger.
Chasing the same missing warehouse document across three sites.
today.time_sinks: The file waits on sites and on the three staffing agencies, and several versions of the same tie-out sit in the folder.

lenses.faster: The population, the sample and the tie-out to the ledger are prepared from AFAS with the selection rule written on the file. Building the sample workbook disappears.
lenses.autonomous: A new auditor request, or a posting on a watch-list, opens the file and lists the missing documents. Manual journals, late revenue and agency invoices without hours are the watch-list.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, journals, VAT codes, three-way match and bank reconciliations would be tested on the full population every month, and the year-end sample would be a check on that work.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses renaming files to a request list. The work worth keeping is explaining a real cutoff or VAT judgment to the auditor.
lenses.options: Each finding can carry three responses: correct the posting, disagree with the evidence attached, or add a compensating check, each with the effect on the audit-adjustment count.
lenses.altitude: The controller maintains the control list and the monthly tests, and reviews the exceptions that go to the auditor.
reach: The sample tie-outs the bookkeepers now prepare for the auditor.
A first draft of the management-letter replies the finance director now writes.
A clear request to the payroll specialist for wage-cost totals, leaving employee detail in AFAS.

tasks.human_edge: What the company states to the statutory auditor and to the Belastingdienst, and whether a finding is accepted.
tasks.pattern_why: Samples and tie-outs follow written rules and come out of AFAS. Anything sent outside the company is a statement of the company, so the controller approves the file first. The external accountant forms the opinion.

in_practice.trigger: The external auditor opens a request, the Belastingdienst asks for support, or a watch-list posting appears during the month.
steps: Build the population from AFAS and draw the sample with the selection rule stored on the file.
Tie each item to the invoice, the contract, the proof of delivery or the Rabobank line.
List documents still missing from the sites or the staffing agencies.
The controller reviews the exceptions and sends the file.
Log the finding and the management response against the control it belongs to.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller approves every file before it is sent. The external accountant remains responsible for the opinion in the wettelijke controle.
data_needed: A locked trial balance and the journal listing
Revenue cutoff support and agency hour backing
VAT codes on transport invoices
The bank reconciliation and the payment-batch log
in_practice.logs_to: The year's audit folder on SharePoint, with sample parameters, the sender and the date.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit can produce an XML auditfile of the ledger in the Dutch auditfile format that auditors and the Belastingdienst use.
MindBridge analyses a full general-ledger population and flags unusual entries for auditors.
Whether Noordhaven's external accountant will rely on a company-drawn sample depends on the engagement, and is untested here.

risks: A tie-out that does not reperform will add findings.
Full-population tests can flood the close with false exceptions and create false comfort.
Payroll and flex-worker lines in a sample are personal data under the AVG and stay restricted to the people who already handle them.
The EU AI Act does not move the auditor's duty. A model output is company preparation, and the accountant does their own work.
research_questions: Will the external accountant accept a sample if the selection parameters are stored with the file?
How many points in last year's management letter were missing documents, and how many were judgments?
Can AFAS produce a complete auditfile that includes the warehouse cutoff and the agency accrual, or do those still sit in Excel?
How many employee-level lines would a normal sample contain, and who is allowed to see them?

tasks.short: Write the rules for budgets, payments, credit and the ledger.

today.trigger: An audit finding, a new agency or bank process, a failed close step, or the annual tidy-up of the finance manual.
steps: Read the old Word procedure and ask the bookkeepers how the work is actually done.
Check who can post, approve and release a Rabobank batch in AFAS.
Draft the rule for budget changes, credit limits, journals and the close.
The finance director signs it and the file is stored on SharePoint.
Tell the team, and later discover that AFAS rights were never changed to match.
drudgery: Rewriting the same control in the manual, the checklist and the mail to the team.
Formatting and versioning Word documents.
Comparing a signed procedure with who really has the AFAS role.
today.time_sinks: The last signed version is hard to find, and it describes screens and roles that AFAS no longer uses.

lenses.faster: A first draft comes out of the house template, the last signed text and the current AFAS authorisation export. Reformatting and hand-comparing roles disappear.
lenses.autonomous: A change in AFAS rights, a new payment-batch type or a new audit finding opens a draft revision. The quarterly review does not depend on someone remembering the manual.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, procure-to-pay, order-to-cash, the close and the forecast would each have a one-page control that matches live AFAS roles and is reviewed every quarter.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses chasing version numbers. The work worth keeping is deciding which risk a team of ten will really manage in close week.
lenses.options: Each control can be drawn up in a tight form with two approvers, a practical form with a detective check, and a minimal form that accepts the risk and logs it, with the effect on days to close, invoices without touch and days sales outstanding.
lenses.altitude: The controller keeps the control catalogue and the test that the written rule still matches AFAS rights, and reviews the gaps.
reach: The credit-limit rules the credit and collections officer now keeps in mail.
The close checklist the accountants now keep in Excel.
The Rabobank batch steps the bookkeepers follow from habit.

tasks.human_edge: The risk a finance team of ten can actually carry, and the finance director's decision to adopt the rule.
tasks.pattern_why: The draft can be nearly complete from the template and the live AFAS rights. It is a company rule only after the finance director approves it, and after the works council route where the rule changes work on the floor.

in_practice.trigger: An audit finding, a change in AFAS authorisations or in the Rabobank batches, a new agency flow, or the quarterly review of the catalogue.
steps: Compare the signed procedure with the AFAS authorisation export and the close checklist.
Draft the revision: objective, AFAS role, evidence, frequency, and the compensating check where full segregation is impossible.
Attach two other workable designs and the effect on days to close, touchless invoices and days sales outstanding.
Route the draft to the controller and then to the finance director.
Publish the approved version on SharePoint and retire the old one.
in_practice.human_gate: The finance director approves every procedure before it is in force. Where a procedure changes how warehouse or HR staff work, the works council is consulted before it is issued.
data_needed: The signed procedures and the close checklist
The AFAS authorisation export
Who can release a Rabobank payment batch
The last management letter
in_practice.logs_to: The controlled-documents library on SharePoint, with version, approver and date.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit holds authorisation by function, including who may post, approve a purchase invoice and release a payment.
Microsoft 365 Copilot in Word can draft and revise a procedure from documents already stored in the tenant.
Power Automate can route a SharePoint document for approval and keep the decision with the file.

risks: A fluent procedure that does not match AFAS rights is a false control and a worse audit finding.
A segregation design that ten people cannot operate in close week will be bypassed on the first busy day.
A rule that directs warehouse or HR staff can require works council advice or consent under the WOR before it is imposed.
Delegation of authority is a management decision. The draft does not set a limit by itself.
research_questions: How many differences are there today between the signed procedures and the AFAS authorisation export?
Which failed controls in the last management letter were missing, and which were written and not operated?
Which draft rules would change warehouse or HR work enough to go to the works council?
Which compensating checks can a team of ten actually run during close week?

tasks.short: Prepare the year-end figures so the adviser can file the tax return.

today.trigger: The year-end ledger is closed and the external adviser sends the information request for the vennootschapsbelasting return.
steps: Export the trial balance from AFAS and rebuild the commercial-to-fiscal bridge in Excel.
List depreciation differences, non-deductible costs, mixed costs and provisions.
Tie wage cost in the ledger to the payroll returns with the payroll specialist.
Summarise the VAT returns and any suppletie, and send the pack to the adviser.
Answer follow-up questions and read the draft return before it is filed.
drudgery: Copying account codes into last year's bridge.
Retyping permanent differences that did not change.
Collecting invoices for small non-deductible items.
today.time_sinks: The trial balance still moves after it was called final, and the wage-cost tie-out waits on payroll.

lenses.faster: Once the year-end periods lock, the trial balance, the fiscal bridge and the tie-out to the VAT returns and the wage-cost totals are assembled from the mapping. Rebuilding the Excel bridge disappears.
lenses.autonomous: Locking the year-end periods opens the pack and lists movements on timing and permanent differences. The controller starts from that list when the adviser writes.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, the fiscal bridge would be kept every month, so the tax line in the forecast is the number the return will use, and a VAT suppletie is found before the Belastingdienst raises it.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses copying the trial balance into a workbook. The work worth keeping is the review with the adviser of the few lines that change the tax.
lenses.options: The pack can show two or three acceptable treatments of a provision, a depreciation life or a claim, with cash tax and the effective rate for each.
lenses.altitude: The controller maintains the mapping from AFAS accounts to fiscal categories and reviews the lines the mapping cannot classify.
reach: The wage-cost tie-out at totals level that now sits between the payroll specialist and the adviser.
A tax figure for the FP&A analysts that uses the same bridge as the return.
The fixed-asset fiscal values that the depreciation work should already have on the register.

tasks.human_edge: The fiscal positions, and the sign-off that the pack matches the locked ledger and can go to the adviser.
tasks.pattern_why: The bridge is a structured roll-forward of a locked ledger. Filing the return is a legal act, so the controller releases the pack and the external adviser signs the return.

in_practice.trigger: The year-end periods are locked in AFAS, or the external adviser issues the annual information request.
steps: Export the locked trial balance and the VAT return totals.
Roll the commercial result through the approved mapping to the vennootschapsbelasting bridge.
Tie wage-cost totals in the ledger to the payroll returns, without employee-level lines.
List open judgments: provisions, mixed costs and VAT on cross-border transport.
The controller reviews the pack, sends it, and reviews the adviser's draft return before filing.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller releases the pack against the locked ledger. The adviser signs the return. A person at the company approves the filing.
data_needed: The locked trial balance and the commercial-to-fiscal mapping
VAT returns and suppleties
Payroll totals reconciled to the ledger
Fiscal values from the fixed-asset register
Last year's filed bridge
in_practice.logs_to: The year's tax folder on SharePoint, with the ledger lock date and the pack version that was sent.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit produces the trial balance, the VAT administration and the financial statements that a corporate-tax pack starts from.
Nextens, used by Dutch tax practices, prepares and files the vennootschapsbelasting return from client figures.
The vennootschapsbelasting return and the jaarrekening are filed in fixed electronic formats, so the adviser's pack is a reconciliation to those figures.

risks: A bridge on a ledger that is still moving can understate or overstate taxable profit, with interest and penalties once filed.
A calculated line can hide a judgment on a provision or a VAT place-of-supply point. The adviser still has to take that position.
The wage reconciliation uses totals. Employee-level payroll data stays in AFAS under the AVG.
Under the EU AI Act the filing duty stays with the company and the adviser. A person approves the return before it is sent.
research_questions: How many lines in last year's bridge were a standing mapping, and how many were one-off judgments?
Does the year-end trial balance stay locked while the adviser works?
Which lines did the adviser change after receiving last year's pack, and why?
Can the wage tie-out be done on AFAS payroll totals without an employee-level export?

tasks.short: Work out the tax the company will pay on the forecast and large buys.

today.trigger: The budget cycle starts, FP&A issues a new forecast, or a large capex or lease request needs a cash and tax view.
steps: Take the forecast profit and apply last year's fiscal differences in Excel.
Test one or two ideas, such as the timing of a provision or the life of a fleet investment, with the adviser.
Check whether any current investment incentive applies before relying on it.
Write a note for the finance director and put a tax-cash line in the forecast.
Revise the line again when the forecast profit moves.
drudgery: Rebuilding the tax-cash line for every forecast version.
Searching mail for the adviser's memo from last year.
Recalculating depreciation differences that the asset register should already hold.
today.time_sinks: The tax line is finished late, so the forecast the business sees carries a stale cash-tax figure.

lenses.faster: Each new forecast version gets a cash-tax line from the approved fiscal bridge, including the loss position and the standing depreciation differences. Rebuilding that sheet disappears.
lenses.autonomous: When FP&A stores a forecast version, the tax-cash line recalculates and the movements are listed. A capex request over the threshold opens a one-page comparison. Both wait for the controller.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, every material truck, racking, fit-out or WMS decision would be priced buy-versus-lease on cash, vennootschapsbelasting and BTW before the order is placed, and the forecast would carry a tax line the adviser would recognise.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses maintaining a side spreadsheet of tax cash. The work worth keeping is choosing a position the company can explain to the Belastingdienst.
lenses.options: Each case can show buy, finance lease and operating lease, or recognising a provision this year or next, with cash, VPB and BTW, and a note of the treatments the adviser has already refused.
lenses.altitude: The controller sets the planning rules and the boundary of positions that always go to the adviser, and checks that the model still uses this year's rules.
reach: The tax-cash line inside the forecast the FP&A analysts maintain.
The employer-cost effect of a werkkostenregeling change, worked with the compensation and benefits specialist.
A capex case for the finance director before a site orders a fleet or a racking project.

tasks.human_edge: Which legal position the company is willing to take and to have the adviser sign.
tasks.pattern_why: The arithmetic can follow an approved bridge. The planning choice is a legal position under rules that change, and the controller leads it with the adviser.

in_practice.trigger: FP&A stores a new forecast version, or a capex or lease request comes in over the threshold.
steps: Apply the approved fiscal bridge to forecast profit and compute cash tax.
For a large purchase, price buy, finance lease and operating lease on cash, VPB and BTW.
Mark any position outside the boundary the adviser has already agreed.
The controller writes the recommendation and the finance director decides.
Write the accepted tax-cash line into that forecast version.
in_practice.human_gate: No tax figure enters the forecast the business sees until the controller accepts it. Anything outside the agreed boundary waits for the adviser.
data_needed: Forecast profit by site
The approved commercial-to-fiscal bridge and the loss position
Asset classes and the capex or lease request
The adviser's latest memo and the incentive rules the adviser has confirmed for this year
in_practice.logs_to: The forecast version history, with the tax note and the controller's initials.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit can report the commercial result by period, which is the starting point for a tax-cash estimate.
A controller can roll an approved fiscal bridge over a forecast in a spreadsheet. The quality depends on the mapping and on this year's rules.
Dutch loss carry-forward, fiscal depreciation limits and investment incentives change in tax plans and have to be confirmed for the year in question before anyone codes them.

risks: A tax line the adviser has not seen can enter the forecast and then miss the filed return, which breaks forecast trust.
An incentive coded from last year's memo can be wrong for this year's trucks or racking.
A structure the model describes still has to pass the adviser and, where it is aggressive, the board. Fraus legis is a legal judgment.
Unpublished fiscal positions stay inside the tenant and the adviser's channel.
research_questions: Which tax positions changed cash or the effective rate over the last three years, and which stayed theoretical?
Does today's forecast tax line reconcile to the last filed return, and by how much?
Which planned assets, if any, qualify for a current fiscal incentive, confirmed in writing by the adviser?
Will the finance director put a tax-cash scenario in the forecast before the adviser has initialled it?

tasks.short: Set depreciation lives and advise whether to buy, lease or sell an asset.

today.trigger: Accounts payable capitalises an invoice, a site sells or scraps a truck or forklift, or a lease quote needs a view before a purchase.
steps: Read the invoice and pick an asset class, a commercial life and a residual value.
Enter the asset in AFAS and set a fiscal life, often in a side calculation.
Check that the fixed-asset subledger still ties to the general ledger.
For a material item, build a buy-versus-lease or keep-versus-replace sheet in Excel.
Tell the site and FP&A what depreciation and cash to expect.
drudgery: Keying lives onto assets that belong in a class with a standard life.
Reconciling the register to the ledger by site.
Rebuilding the same lease comparison for another forklift or trailer.
today.time_sinks: Lives were set once and never revised, and the fiscal value often lives in the year-end Excel file rather than on the asset.

lenses.faster: An invoice that matches an approved class takes that class's commercial life, residual, fiscal life and ledger accounts. The controller stops rating each forklift, trailer and racking line.
lenses.autonomous: Capitalising a purchase invoice proposes the class. Repeat assets in an approved class depreciate on the register. A disposal recorded by a site opens the gain or loss and parks it if it is over the threshold.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, every asset at the three sites would carry a current economic life, and idle trucks and forklifts would be visible before the company orders another one.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses keying a life onto a repeat asset. The work worth keeping is the keep-or-replace call on a fleet, made with the site.
lenses.options: A material request can show buy, finance lease and operating lease, or extend the life versus replace, with depreciation, fiscal deduction, cash and the site result.
lenses.altitude: The controller maintains the class policy and the capitalisation threshold, and deals with new classes, changed lives, impairments and material disposals.
reach: Capitalise-or-expense calls that the bookkeepers now make alone on supplier invoices.
Depreciation and capex for the FP&A forecast, taken from the register.
A list of idle assets for the site leads before a new truck or forklift is ordered.

tasks.human_edge: A new class, a change of useful life, an impairment, and the buy, lease or sell decision on a material asset.
tasks.pattern_why: Life, residual value and method sit on the asset class, and AFAS posts the amount from those rules, with no model in the path. The controller handles the exceptions and the advice above the threshold.

in_practice.trigger: Accounts payable capitalises a purchase invoice, a site records a disposal, or a lease quote arrives.
steps: Match the invoice to an asset class and propose commercial life, residual, fiscal life and ledger accounts.
Post depreciation for assets in a class the controller has already approved.
Park a new class, a change of life, an impairment, a component split, a material lease and a disposal over the threshold.
Attach the cash and result comparison for a parked buy, lease or sell.
The controller decides the exception and the outcome is sent to the site and to FP&A.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller approves each new class, any change of life, any impairment, and every buy, lease or sell above the threshold. Repeat assets in an approved class post on their own.
data_needed: The asset-class policy and the capitalisation threshold
Whether the jaarrekening is under RJ or IFRS, and the fiscal lives the adviser has accepted
Lease quotes and disposal proceeds
The fixed-asset subledger and the general-ledger balance
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS asset record for routine postings, and a one-page memo in the SharePoint capex folder for every exception.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit vaste activa calculates and posts depreciation from the asset's method, useful life and residual value.
A fixed-asset subledger in AFAS can be reconciled to the general ledger by period.
Buy-versus-lease advice for a Dutch logistics fleet still depends on the reporting framework and on the fiscal lives the adviser accepts. Those are not confirmed for this company.

risks: One wrong class repeats in the monthly depreciation and in the fiscal bridge until the audit finds it.
Commercial and fiscal lives have to stay separate. Using one life for both misstates either the jaarrekening or the return.
Lease classification under Dutch GAAP is a judgment on a material contract. The calculation can be prepared, and the controller signs it.
A significant fleet or racking investment can be a matter for works council advice under the WOR. A single forklift is not.
This task is about 32 hours a year. The saving is real only if classes are inconsistent or fiscal lives sit in Excel.
research_questions: How many asset records are there, in how many classes, and how often does the posted life differ from the class policy?
Does the register reconcile to the ledger at each site, and are fiscal values stored on the asset?
Is the jaarrekening prepared under RJ or IFRS, and are material leases still classified in Excel?
How many capitalised invoices last year were repeats of an existing class?

role.altitude: The controller stops rebuilding bridges, sample files and procedures, and becomes the owner of the definitions, the asset classes, the fiscal mapping and the control catalogue. The job is to keep the close short and the forecast trustworthy, and to sign the exceptions.
reach: The first-pass monthly variance that the FP&A analysts now assemble.
Capitalise-or-expense decisions and auditor tie-outs that the bookkeepers now prepare.
The credit-limit framework that the credit and collections officer now applies from mail.
The wage-cost-to-ledger reconciliation at totals level, now split between the payroll specialist and the tax adviser.
The close checklist and the flux comments that the accountants now keep in Excel.
A first draft of management-letter responses for the finance director.
role.ceiling_note: There is one controller. Close week and the year-end tax pack still bunch the hours, and the adviser, the statutory auditor and the works council set waiting time this person does not control. A finance team of ten limits how far segregation can go. Filings, management representations and fiscal positions stay with a named person. Payroll detail and poortwachter files stay with HR and payroll under the AVG, so the controller works from totals. Drafting speed is not the ceiling. The ceiling is the number of judgments that still need this person.
skills_to_grow: Write a control so an AFAS authorisation export can show whether it operates.
Keep one commercial-to-fiscal mapping and one asset-class policy that the ledger and the return both use.
Review a drafted variance, sample and tax bridge and find the line that is wrong.
Know which positions belong with the external adviser or the statutory auditor.
State a result in site language: flex premium, dock overtime, claims and truck lives.
Run the works council information and advice route when a decision is a significant investment.
role.ambitious_version: The ledger, the fiscal bridge, the asset register and the control tests are current every month. Agency, claims and depreciation accruals are proposed before anyone asks, so days to close fall. The forecast the business sees carries a cause, a cash effect and a tax effect that finance has signed, which is how forecast accuracy, days sales outstanding, invoices without touch and audit adjustments move together. The controller spends the saved hours on the few points that change the result: site contribution, flex versus own staff, capex, and the items the auditor will challenge.
